w10_T4_005347: Elena brought 145 printed sheets to the craft market, and every sheet is perforated into 5 postcards. Her partner Dmitri, whose own pile was smaller than hers, contributed 45 loose postcards. The pitch costs 90 a week to rent. Over the weekend 310 postcards were sold to visitors, and 25 came back from a shop that had not sold them. Half of the designs are of the harbour. Each postcard still unsold was slipped into a pack with 4 envelopes, and 110 of those envelopes were creased and thrown away. How many envelopes did Elena have?
w10_T4_005349: Marco was given 108 chocolate bars for the school trip. He shared them equally with his sister Lena, who had brought none of her own, so each of them took half. Every bar in Marco's share is scored into 7 small squares. The children on the coach ate 223 of Marco's squares before the ferry. At the hotel he was handed 76 more squares from an opened box. How many squares did Marco have?
w10_T4_005357: The cattery had 125 tins of cat food in its store, and it gives all feeding amounts in grams rather than in kilograms. A long busy fortnight used up 120 of the tins. The cattery has 18 pens along the south wall. A wholesaler then delivered 44 tins, and the owner bought 76 more at a cash and carry. Over the following month 91 tins were opened. Each tin still in the store provides 2 meals. How many meals are in the store?
w10_T4_005363: The car showroom opened the morning with 150 test-drive slots free in its diary. Bookings taken over the phone before ten o'clock filled 108 of them. The showroom stocks 24 different models. A run of cancellations freed up 11 slots again just before lunch. Walk-in customers took 40 slots during the afternoon. In the evening an online promotion filled another 11 slots. How many slots were still free?
w10_T4_005372: The wire depot counted 203 rolls in the yard when it opened in the morning, and a supplier dropped off 10 more before eight. A dozen workers were on the early shift. Every roll on the rack is drawn out into 9 straight lengths. During the afternoon each length was chopped into 4 shorter pieces on the bench saw. In the evening every piece was bent into 4 hooks for the garden centre order. How many hooks did the depot make?
w10_T4_005374: Nadia filled 45 baking boxes in the morning, and each box held 7 almond pastries. Her colleague Emre, who had produced far fewer that day, added 23 pastries from his own tray. During the afternoon every pastry was cut into 5 tasting pieces for the food festival. In the evening the visitors ate 494 of those pieces before the stall closed. How many tasting pieces were left on the stall?
w10_T4_005384: Priya had 180 sheets of coloured foil for the decorations. Her friend Jacob, who had bought less than she had, handed over 50 sheets from his bag. Half of the foil is gold. Every sheet was cut into 7 long strips. Each strip was folded into 9 paper stars for the hall. Every star then had to be held together with 6 stitches of thread. How many stitches were needed?
w10_T4_005390: The courier depot loaded 120 parcels into its bay at the start of the day, and it quotes delivery windows in minutes rather than in hours. The parcels were split equally among the 4 rounds, and the supervisor followed the van doing the morning round. That driver collected 73 further parcels from a business park. She then delivered 29 parcels along the ring road. A second pick-up put 66 more parcels into her van. Before returning she delivered 116 parcels around the housing estate. How many parcels were still in her van?
w10_T4_005396: Ida had 199 seed packets stored in her potting shed. Her neighbour Omar, whose shelf held far fewer than hers, gave her 33 packets he would never use, and the garden shop threw in 12 more with an order. Every packet held enough for 2 sowings, so Ida relabelled her stock as that many single sowings. She used 409 of the sowings across her beds in the spring, and 1 more was ruined when a mouse got into the shed. Late in the year she was given 22 further sowings by the allotment society. How many sowings did Ida have?
w10_T4_005401: The school kitchen had 198 lunch trays stacked in the morning, and it measures its portions in millilitres rather than in litres. Half of the trays were driven over to the annexe, and half stayed in the main hall. The caretaker found 24 of the remaining trays cracked and skipped them. A supplier delivered 54 new trays before the first sitting. During the afternoon each tray in the hall was set with 3 bowls for the after-school club. In the evening every bowl was filled with 3 scoops of soup. How many scoops of soup were served?
w10_T4_005404: The print works has 88 rolls of paper in its store, and every roll is cut into 8 large sheets. The print hall has 12 tall windows along one side, and poster sizes are quoted in millimetres rather than in centimetres. Each sheet is printed with 9 posters before trimming. The finished posters were shared equally among the 4 cities in the campaign, and the manager tracked only the batch bound for Bristol. Of that batch, 86 posters were creased in transit and destroyed. How many posters reached Bristol in good condition?
w10_T4_005405: Amina opened her workroom in the morning with 219 rolls of curtain fabric, and she measures every length in centimetres rather than in metres. She sold 39 rolls to a hotel buyer before lunch. Each roll still on the shelf was cut into 8 panels. During the afternoon 1197 panels were sewn up into finished curtains and sent out. In the evening every panel that remained was decorated with 9 glass beads, and her colleague Tobias, who kept a smaller bead box than hers, contributed 50 loose beads. How many beads were in the workroom?
w10_T4_005408: Ryo had 44 unbuilt model kits stacked in his cupboard, and the shop sells its paint in millilitres rather than in litres. He gave 27 of the kits to his cousin Nina, who had none at all. Every kit still in the cupboard contains 5 plastic sprues, and each sprue holds 6 separate parts. The club meets for 2 hours on a Thursday. Ryo found 13 loose parts at the bottom of the cupboard, and Nina returned 51 parts she did not need. How many parts did Ryo have?
w10_T4_005413: The festival printed 203 posters for the first weekend, and the print run was then doubled so that twice as many existed. Every poster carries 5 tear-off tabs along its lower edge, and all times on them are given in minutes rather than in hours. The office found 75 loose tabs in a drawer and 20 more in the volunteers' folder, and counted them with the rest. Over the festival 1271 tabs were torn off by people passing. How many tabs were left?
w10_T4_005415: The garage had 121 tyres stacked behind the workshop. An inspection condemned 4 of them and they went for scrap. Customers traded in 15 part-worn tyres over the month, and a wholesaler delivered 77 new ones. The fitters put 114 tyres onto customer cars during the same period. Every tyre still in the stack has to be stored with 4 wheel nuts taped to it. How many wheel nuts does the stack need?
w10_T4_005416: Farah had 208 blank discs ready for the archive project. Her colleague Owen, whose own supply was smaller, handed her 77 discs from the media room. Testing showed 38 of the discs to be faulty and they were binned. Every good disc holds 4 recorded albums from the collection. A licensing review forced the archive to delete 298 of those albums. Owen then supplied 58 further albums from his own tapes. How many albums does the archive hold?
w10_T4_005417: The school ordered 176 revision guides for the exam season, and the term lasts 14 weeks. The guides were shared equally among the 4 year groups, and the head of maths worked only with the set given to Year 11. Every guide in that set is divided into 5 topic sections, and half of them are on algebra. The class had already covered 98 of those sections in lessons before Easter, and the teacher dropped 5 sections as too advanced. Each remaining section needs 3 lessons to teach. How many lessons are needed?
w10_T4_005419: The city planted 207 street trees along the new avenue last winter and added 43 more in the spring. Half of them are limes. The avenue itself runs for 3 kilometres. By May every tree carried 9 flowering branches. Each branch opened with 8 blossoms in the warm week that followed. A night of storms then brought down 9117 blossoms onto the pavements. How many blossoms were still on the trees?
w10_T4_005420: Selin drew 19 comic strips for the school magazine. She looked them over and threw away 7 that she had never finished. She then shared the finished strips equally with her co-editor Kaan, who had drawn none himself, so each of them took half. The printer sent Selin 78 further strips submitted by other pupils, and she added them to her own set. Every strip in her set is laid out across 2 magazine pages. How many magazine pages does Selin's set fill?
w10_T4_005427: The jam kitchen filled 184 jars for the county show. Every jar had to be labelled in 3 languages, so the number of labels needed tripled. Her partner Ana, who had printed more labels than the kitchen expected, supplied 69 of them, and a village shop sent 52 spares. The kitchen has 6 preserving pans. In the end 493 labels were stuck onto jars and boxes. How many labels were left over?
w10_T4_005429: The community workshop had 213 sheets of plywood in its rack. A stage-building job used 64 of them over the winter. A timber merchant delivered 67 sheets in February, and a closing factory donated 44 more. The workshop is open 5 days a week. Every sheet in the rack was cut into 4 shelf boards for the housing project. Damp in the store warped 75 of the boards and they were rejected. How many shelf boards were usable?
w10_T4_005431: Bruno came back from the coast with 25 boxes of shells, and each box held 8 shells. His sister Carla, who had filled far more boxes than he had, gave him 79 shells from her own collection. He found 15 of his shells broken when he unpacked them and threw those away. A second trip added 71 shells to the tray. The walk to the beach takes 40 minutes. Every shell in the tray was threaded onto a cord with 3 wooden beads. How many wooden beads did Bruno use?
w10_T4_005436: The roastery opened the morning with 193 sacks of coffee, and every sack is split into 8 retail bags. A dozen baristas came in for the training session. The sample room sent up 9 extra bags, and the roasting floor added 9 more that had been held back for testing. The company weighs its coffee in grams rather than in kilograms. In the evening the manager worked out that each bag brews 4 full pots. How many pots of coffee would the stock brew?
w10_T4_005439: The estate has 133 rows of vines, with 9 vines standing in every row, and it measures its juice in litres rather than in hectolitres. Each vine carried 7 bunches of grapes this September. Half of the estate faces south. Mildew spoiled 309 of the bunches before picking, and the press took 4315 bunches during the first week of the harvest. The estate covers 22 hectares in all. The trial plot behind the barn contributed 47 further bunches. How many bunches were left unpressed?
w10_T4_005441: The museum has 221 display cases, and every case holds 8 exhibits. The curator Leah brought up 68 further exhibits from the basement store, rather more than her colleague Tom had managed to find. Each exhibit on show was photographed 3 times for the new catalogue. The picture editor rejected 4598 of those photographs as too dark to print. How many photographs were kept for the catalogue?
